To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the branching ratio of $B_c \rightarrow D_s^*(2110) \gamma$ in the TCMLSM is $1.2 \times 10^{-6}$ which is 2.4 times smaller than that in the SM.
the $B_c \rightarrow D_s^*$ radiative decay is dominated by the weak annihilation mechanism.

the $B_c \rightarrow D_s^*(2317)\gamma$ transition amplitude is enhanced by a factor of 1.5 in the TCMLSM with respect to the SM, which is mainly due to the enhancement of the $B_c$ wave function at the origin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the rare radiative decays $B_c \rightarrow D_s^*(D_s) \gamma$ in the TCMLSM.
the rare radiative $B_c\to D_s^*γ$ decay.
the rare radiative process $B_c \rightarrow D_s^*$, which can be measured at future $B$-factories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the $B_c \rightarrow D_s^*$ process is very sensitive to the underlying theory of electroweak interactions.

the $B_c$ meson is a very promising candidate for testing the TCMLSM and the SM, since the $b$-quark decay is a clean and well understood process, and the $B_c \rightarrow D_s^*$ is an excellent candidate for the study of $B_c$ physics.
the $B_c \rightarrow D_s^*$ radiative decay is not sensitive to the TCMLSM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the branching ratio for $B_c\to D_s^* + \gamma$ in the TCMLSM is larger than that in the SM.
the $B_c \rightarrow D_s^*(\rightarrow D_s\pi)$ decay is a good place for searching for the new physics beyond the SM.
the TCMLSM is not excluded by the present data on $B_c\to D_s^*{\rm (or}D_s^*) \gamma$.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the TCMLSM with scalars, the $B_c \rightarrow D_s^*(D_s) \gamma$ process is not suppressed, and is comparable to that in the SM.
the $B_c \rightarrow D_s^*$ transition is not a good place to probe the TCMLSM.
the $B_c$ meson is a good probe of the technicolor with scalons.
